title: Japan's Envoy Gets a Taste of Bollywood Magic at Mumbai's Film City
excerpt: Ambassador ONO Keiichi toured Mumbai's Film City on Wednesday, posing at the Wall of Fame and pledging deeper India-Japan entertainment ties ahead of the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027.
body:
• Japanese Ambassador to India ONO Keiichi visited Mumbai's Film City on October 7, posing near the complex's popular "Wall of Fame" and sharing glimpses of the trip on X.
  • He called for deeper India-Japan cooperation in the entertainment industry as the two countries prepare to mark the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027.
  • According to the Ministry of External Affairs, 2027 will be observed as the India-Japan Year of Shared Horizons, with the week of April 28 designated India-Japan Week.
  • The visit continues a tradition of Bollywood outreach by Japanese envoys: former ambassador Hiroshi Suzuki went viral in 2024 for dancing to Hindi film songs at the same studio complex.

Japan's ambassador to India spent Wednesday immersed in Bollywood. ONO Keiichi toured Mumbai's Film City — one of India's largest film studio complexes — posting photos from the visit on his X account, including one taken beside the complex's "Wall of Fame," a gallery of characters and personalities associated with Hindi cinema.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=M4uc9VIi58o

According to ANI, Ono said he was excited to witness Bollywood production firsthand and experience the country's vibrant film industry. He used the occasion to pitch closer creative ties between the two countries ahead of a major milestone: the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations in 2027.

"Visited Film City Mumbai. Thrilled to witness firsthand the production of Bollywood films and experience the very essence of Indian cinema. Looking forward to deepening our cooperation in the entertainment industry as we mark the 75th anniversary of relations next year!"

— ONO Keiichi, Japanese Ambassador to India

A growing tradition of cultural diplomacy

Ono's visit follows a playbook his predecessor turned into a phenomenon. Former ambassador Hiroshi Suzuki built a large social media following through his enthusiastic engagement with Indian culture — riding a Mumbai local train like a daily commuter, sampling street food in Pune (he asked for "thoda teekha kam," a little less spicy), and in March 2024 touring Film City himself, posing with props from Aamir Khan's "3 Idiots" and writing that he "felt like Aamir Khan." A video of Suzuki dancing to Bollywood music drew cheers from Indian users, and singer Shilpa Rao publicly thanked him after he danced to her hit "Kaavaalaa" in 2023.

Why Bollywood resonates in Japan

Indian cinema has a genuine, if niche, following in Japan. Rajinikanth commands a devoted Japanese fan base — a promotional tour for his film "Kochadaiiyaan" was planned around a Tokyo visit — and Bollywood films have long found festival and arthouse audiences there. The exchange runs both ways: acclaimed anime director Makoto Shinkai traveled to Mumbai for the Indian theatrical release of "Suzume" in April 2023, a visit described at the time as a milestone for cultural ties between the two countries.

The road to 2027

The Film City visit lands in the run-up to a significant anniversary year. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, India and Japan will celebrate 2027 as the India-Japan Year of Shared Horizons, with commemorative programs held across both countries and special participation from the youth of India and Japan. The week of April 28, 2027, will be designated India-Japan Week to mark the establishment of diplomatic relations.

What this means for the diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, these cultural exchanges are a quiet signal of how India's creative industries are woven into its foreign policy. Entertainment cooperation opens doors for co-productions, film exchanges, and artist residencies — and gives Indians in Japan a visible cultural bridge to the country they live in. With anime already massively popular among young Indians and Bollywood's footprint growing in Japan, the two countries' creative industries look poised for a deeper partnership.

What's next

Watch for entertainment to feature prominently in the 2027 anniversary calendar: joint film programs, creative-industry delegations, and possibly India-Japan co-productions. Ono has made people-to-people ties a theme of his tenure, and his social media presence suggests more such cultural forays are on the way.
